Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
557 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonably hot with highs in the 90s and heat index values
  100-107F each day.
  
- An isolated late day shower can't be ruled out along the
  seabreeze later today.
  
- Slightly better rain chances expected Thursday into early next
  week for southern parts of the region as some deeper moisture
  flows back inland. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1132 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

Ridging centered over the Southwest CONUS/Four Corners is expected 
to result in largely uneventful weather over SE Texas through early 
next week at least. The ridge is anticipated to drift north slightly 
beginning Thursday with heights and 850mb temperatures expected to 
drop slightly into the weekend, resulting in a slight downturn in 
heat stress. Decreasing subsidence and rising PWs should bring some 
better rain chances throughout this period, with isolated 
seabreeze/baybreeze showers/storms becoming more scattered in nature 
as a result, especially after today. Overall highs will be in the 
90s each day with heat indices reaching the triple digits in the 
afternoon. Some patchy fog will be possible during the early morning 
hours.

03

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 557 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Current satellite imagery depicts MVFR/IFR ceilings developing
over areas along and west of the Brazos River. These reduced
ceilings are anticipated to move into CLL and UTS over the next
couple of hours and may extend into CXO and IAH as well later this
morning. Additionally, periods of patchy fog have brought reduced
visibility to LBX as well. Based on yesterday, SGR may also experience
reduced visibility for a few hours around and shortly after 
sunrise. 

VFR conditions will return area-wide by 15Z. Light south-southwest 
winds early this morning will become southerly by the afternoon 
with wind speeds in the 8-12 kt range. Occasional gusts of 15-20
kt will be possible through the afternoon. Isolated SH/TS 
possible again this afternoon between 21Z-01Z mainly around the 
Houston metro terminals. Winds become light and variable 
overnight with potential for another round of patchy fog and 
reduced ceilings mainly west of I-45 going into Thursday morning.
Ceilings/visibilities improve back to VFR by 15Z on Thursday with
south to southeast winds around 8-12 kt prevailing. Another round
of isolated to scattered SH/TS possible in the afternoon.

Batiste

throughout the next several days. Rain chances increase slightly on

showers and storms will be greatest during the late night through 
early afternoon hours for the Gulf.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
624 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A typical summer weather pattern will prevail through this week
  with a few afternoon thunderstorms each day. 

- Afternoon highs will climb into the low to mid 90s each day 
  with maximum heat indices ranging from 101 to 109.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Today through Tuesday)
Issued at 1204 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

The forecast is a persistent one with the day-to-day forecast not
changing much over the next several days. We remain stuck between
a high pressure ridge to the west with a weak upper level low on 
the eastern seaboard. Each day diurnally driven showers and 
thunderstorms should be expected with rain chances between 30 and 
60%. Storm coverage will be sporadic, forming off the sea breeze 
or outflows. Showers will also be slow moving but with PWATs near 
the median values flash flooding isn't a major concern . 

Near the surface high pressure in the eastern Gulf will keep our 
winds light and primarily from the south. During the afternoon the
dry air aloft will mix down to the surface which will lower our 
dew points, keeping heat index values from reaching heat advisory 
levels of +108F. Afternoon highs will be in the mid 90s with 
slightly higher values in central Louisiana. These values are a 
degree or two above the climatological average but not record- 
breaking.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 616 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Showers and low clouds (as well as some ground fog) stubbornly 
hung around through the night across southwest and central 
Louisiana. This area has been situated under a trof axis extending
from low pressure near central Mississippi. Cloud cover and any 
ground fog will likely break up with sunrise, but with this lower 
pressure, expect scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop 
from afternoon to early evening. This is the first of many days 
which should see a return to the typical summertime climo pattern.

A southerly wind will prevail today, particularly in response to
the diurnal breeze cycle. 

11

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1204 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Onshore winds will be between 10 and 15 knots with 2 to 4 feet
waves. Isolated showers will be possible in the afternoons.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1204 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

KBDI values continue to climb. Isolated showers and thunderstorms
are expected each afternoon will provide local relief but 
otherwise no widespread rain is expected. Minimum RH values will
be around 50%.
